story.heading: Our Story
story.body: Can someone start from nothing and build something meaningful? That belief inspired the founding of AGILE — Audit, Advisory, Governance & Leadership Excellence in 2026. Co founded by Chartered Accountants, among them Claudine Simo Mamo, a CEMAC certified Chartered Accountant and Fellow of ACCA, AGILE brings together the collective expertise of its partners while reflecting Claudine's 37 years of leadership in finance and accounting across the CEMAC region. She joined AGILE to mentor young professionals and to build leadership capacity, ownership and accountability within teams. As a strategic advisor to banks, insurers, microfinance institutions and asset managers, she strengthens financial systems, supports regulatory compliance under OHADA, COBAC, CIMA and COSUMAF, and drives performance, particularly in agro industry, banking and microfinance structuring. Her vision is clear: sustainable success comes from strong foundations, discipline and continuous growth. At AGILE we secure value, empower growth and build trust, proving that meaningful futures are built from humble beginnings, one strategic step at a time.

founderBio.heading: Claudine Simo Mamo, Founder and Managing Partner
founderBio.body: Claudine Simo Mamo is a CEMAC certified Chartered Accountant and Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), with over 37 years of experience in audit, accounting and advisory across Central Africa. Her career reflects both discipline and progression. She began in education in 1988, moved into project management, and later joined ECA, where she built her expertise over time. As the firm grew within the Ernst & Young (EY) network, she stepped into leadership, serving as Associate Director and Head of Audit for Cameroon and Chad, leading complex engagements across banking, insurance, asset management, agro industry and utilities. In 2023 she became a Partner at ECA S.A., leading audit, statutory audit, accounting and advisory services for major institutions across the region. Today she operates as an Independent Chartered Accountant and Founder and Managing Partner of AGILE, where she supports institutions and growing organisations in strengthening their systems, improving governance and building sustainable performance. At this stage of her career her focus goes beyond numbers. She is committed to developing people, mentoring young professionals and building a culture of responsibility. This commitment is reflected in her active involvement in the governing bodies of the accounting profession and in women's professional associations across the region.

overview.headline: Expert OHADA Audit and Financial Compliance Services across CEMAC and beyond
overview.intro: Across the CEMAC region and beyond, AGILE delivers OHADA audit services and financial compliance expertise for banks, insurers, agro industry leaders, microfinance institutions and emerging FinTech. We combine rigorous statutory audits, SYSCOHADA certification and COBAC and CIMA risk management to secure assets, ensure regulatory adherence and drive performance. Our approach prioritises reliability, practical advice and value chain protection under the OHADA, COBAC, CIMA and COSUMAF frameworks.
overview.ctaHeadline: Curious what we can do for your organisation?

audit.title: Audit and Assurance Hub (Securing Information)
audit.short: Our Audit and Assurance Hub secures financial information and ensures compliance with OHADA and sector standards. We provide statutory audits for banks, insurers, microfinance institutions and listed entities, accounting systems diagnostics, and contractual audits including due diligence, project reviews and limited assurance. For agro industry we support growth through SYSCOHADA certification, collateral and securities advisory, legal structuring of value chains and PPPs, and ESG compliance audits.
audit.detail: Our Audit and Assurance Hub is designed to secure financial information, strengthen compliance and support informed decisions across regulated and high growth sectors. Our statutory audit services cover banks, insurers, microfinance institutions and listed entities, ensuring annual legal compliance and dependable reporting. We carry out accounting systems diagnostics to assess financial organisation, audit trails, internal controls and the reliability of statements. Our contractual audits include acquisition due diligence, project audits and limited reviews tailored to your objectives and risk profile. For agro industry clients we deliver SYSCOHADA audit and certification for agro industrial complexes, collateral and securities advisory for agricultural financing, and legal structuring for value chain contracts and public and private partnerships. We also integrate ESG compliance audits that identify and manage environmental, social and governance risks. By combining technical precision, regulatory knowledge and practical insight, we help institutions protect assets, improve governance and build long term confidence.
deliverables: Statutory audit (CAC): annual legal audits for banks, insurers, microfinance institutions and listed entities.
Accounting systems diagnostics: review of financial organisation, audit trail and reliability of statements.
Contractual audits: acquisition due diligence, project audits and limited reviews.

faqs.a: Audit and assurance services assess the accuracy, reliability and compliance of financial information and business processes. An audit provides an independent review of records and controls, while assurance gives stakeholders confidence that the information is credible, complete and prepared to the required standard. Together they help businesses improve transparency, reduce risk and strengthen trust.

faqs.q: What are audit and assurance services?
faqs.a: These include independent checks of financial statements, internal controls, compliance and operational processes. They help organisations meet legal and regulatory requirements, identify weaknesses and improve decision making. Common examples include statutory audits, internal audits, compliance reviews and limited assurance engagements. They build confidence among investors, regulators, lenders and management.

faqs.q: What are the main types of audits?
faqs.a: The main types are financial audits, compliance audits, operational audits and forensic audits. Financial audits review statements for accuracy. Compliance audits check whether rules and regulations are followed. Operational audits assess efficiency and effectiveness. Forensic audits investigate suspected fraud or misconduct. Each serves a different purpose in protecting business integrity.

audit.keywords: audit and assurance, statutory audit CAC, types of audits, OHADA audit, financial statement audit

agro.title: Agro Industry Focus: Performance and Security (OHADA Framework)
agro.short: Agro industry is a key growth engine across CEMAC, driving food security, investment and value creation. We support agro industrial businesses through strategic financial planning, restructuring, due diligence and transaction advisory. Our expertise also covers SYSCOHADA audit and certification, collateral and securities advisory, legal structuring of value chain contracts and PPP agreements, and ESG compliance to protect assets, strengthen governance and support sustainable growth.
agro.detail: Agro industry advisory, financial planning and transaction support are essential for sustainable growth across the CEMAC region. We provide expert support to agro industrial businesses, financial institutions and investors seeking to strengthen performance, manage risk and improve value creation. We deliver strategic financial planning, business restructuring, due diligence and transaction advisory tailored to complex commercial and regulatory environments. Our expertise also includes SYSCOHADA audit and certification, collateral and securities advisory, legal structuring and ESG compliance. We support the drafting of value chain contracts and public and private partnership agreements, helping organisations secure assets, improve governance and build resilient operations. By combining sector knowledge, regulatory insight and practical advisory, we help clients drive sustainable growth across the agro industry value chain.
deliverables: Strategic financial planning to support growth and better capital allocation.
Due diligence and transaction advisory to reduce risk and improve decisions.
SYSCOHADA audit and certification for stronger compliance and reporting.
Legal structuring for value chain contracts and PPP agreements.
ESG compliance support to improve governance, transparency and sustainability.

faqs.a: SYSCOHADA is the harmonised accounting system used across OHADA member states in West and Central Africa. It provides common rules for financial reporting, making accounts more consistent, transparent and comparable across businesses and countries. It helps organisations comply with regional accounting requirements while improving the quality and reliability of financial information.

Collateral security is an asset a borrower pledges to a lender to secure a loan. If the borrower fails to repay, the lender can use the asset to recover the debt. It reduces lending risk and can help businesses or individuals access finance more easily. Common examples include land, vehicles, machinery, inventory or other valuable property.

ESG audits are independent reviews of an organisation's environmental, social and governance practices. They assess whether policies, reporting and performance are accurate, responsible and aligned with sustainability standards. ESG audits help businesses identify risks, improve transparency and strengthen trust with investors, regulators and stakeholders.

agro.keywords: SYSCOHADA, collateral security, ESG audits, agro industry OHADA, value chain financing

risk.title: Risk, Actuarial and Sectoral Compliance Hub
risk.short: We deliver specialist expertise across COBAC, CIMA and COSUMAF, supporting banks, microfinance institutions, emerging FinTech, insurers and financial market operators. Our services include insurance technical provisions review, solvency analysis and actuarial pricing; banking risk mapping, stress testing, liquidity management and operational risk prevention; and financial markets compliance audits, internal control systems and independent asset valuations. We also provide AML/CFT compliance support aligned with GABAC standards.
risk.detail: Our specialist regulatory and risk advisory services support financial institutions, insurers, microfinance institutions, emerging FinTech players and capital market operators across the COBAC, CIMA and COSUMAF frameworks. We help organisations navigate complex requirements, strengthen internal controls and improve resilience. In insurance, we provide technical provisions review, solvency analysis and actuarial pricing support to help insurers maintain compliance and sound financial management. For banks and microfinance institutions, and for FinTech operating under COBAC regulation, our services include risk mapping, stress testing, liquidity management and operational risk prevention. In financial markets, we deliver compliance audits, internal control reviews and independent asset valuations to support transparency, accountability and investor trust. We also offer AML/CFT compliance support aligned with GABAC standards, helping institutions implement robust frameworks, strengthen monitoring and reduce exposure to financial crime and regulatory sanctions. By combining technical expertise, regulatory knowledge and practical risk management, we help clients build stronger governance and more sustainable operations.
deliverables: Regulatory compliance support across COBAC, CIMA, COSUMAF and GABAC standards.
Risk tools such as risk mapping, stress testing and liquidity management.
Technical review for insurance provisions, solvency and actuarial pricing.
Compliance audits, internal control checks and independent asset valuations.
AML/CFT framework implementation to reduce financial crime risk and strengthen governance.

faqs.a: COBAC is the Central African Banking Commission. It is the banking supervisory authority for the CEMAC region and oversees credit institutions to ensure compliance with prudential rules, sound banking practice and financial stability. COBAC plays a key role in banking regulation, risk supervision and the protection of depositors across Central Africa.

faqs.q: What are common risk assessment tools?
faqs.a: Risk assessment tools help organisations identify, measure and manage operational, financial, cyber and compliance risks. Common options include qualitative risk matrices, quantitative scoring models, heat maps, checklists, internal control questionnaires and risk management software. The right tool depends on your sector, regulatory environment and the level of detail you need for reporting and decisions.

Compliance audits are independent reviews that check whether an organisation follows laws, regulations, internal policies and industry standards. They confirm that operations, financial processes and governance practices meet required rules. Compliance audits reduce legal risk, improve accountability and strengthen trust with regulators, investors and stakeholders.

risk.keywords: COBAC, risk assessment tools, compliance audits, CIMA solvency, AML CFT GABAC

performance.title: Performance and Management Hub
performance.short: We turn financial data into practical decision tools that support stronger performance and control. Our services include budgeting and monitoring through forecasts, dashboards and variance analysis; tax compliance support with diagnostics, regulatory monitoring and filing assistance; and accounting engineering covering monthly close, consolidation and cost accounting. We help organisations improve efficiency, strengthen compliance and make better informed decisions across all levels of management.
performance.detail: Our financial management and compliance services turn data into practical tools for strategic decisions, stronger control and sustainable performance. We help organisations improve visibility over their finances, strengthen compliance and build systems that support growth and accountability. Through budgeting and monitoring, we provide forecasts, dashboards and variance analysis that give management a clear view of performance against targets, enabling faster decisions and better resource allocation. Our tax compliance support includes diagnostics, regulatory monitoring and filing assistance, helping clients stay current with tax obligations while reducing the risk of penalties and errors. We also offer accounting engineering, including monthly close, consolidation and cost accounting systems that improve reporting accuracy and operational efficiency. Whether the objective is to improve planning, strengthen compliance or enhance reporting, our approach is practical, structured and results oriented, helping clients transform financial data into insight and confident decisions at every level.
deliverables: Budgeting and monitoring: forecasts, dashboards, variance analysis.
Tax compliance: diagnostics, regulatory monitoring and filing assistance.
Accounting engineering: close, consolidation and cost accounting systems.

faqs.a: Budgeting and monitoring is the process of planning income and expenditure, then tracking actual performance against the approved budget. It helps organisations control costs, spot variances early and make informed decisions. In practice it supports better cash flow management, stronger accountability and more accurate forecasting.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of tax compliance in Cameroon?
faqs.a: Tax compliance ensures individuals and businesses meet their legal tax obligations, file accurately and pay on time. It helps avoid penalties, supports government revenue collection and strengthens transparency. Good tax compliance also improves business credibility, reduces regulatory risk and supports long term financial stability.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for tax compliance?
faqs.a: Tax compliance is the responsibility of both the business and its management. Directors, finance teams, accountants and tax advisers all play a role in ensuring accurate records, correct filings and timely payments. In larger organisations responsibility may be shared, but the ultimate duty remains with the taxpayer and its leadership.

performance.keywords: budgeting and monitoring, tax compliance Cameroon, compliance services, accounting engineering

heritage.title: Heritage and Transmission Hub
heritage.short: We help clients secure and enhance professional and personal assets through valuation, diagnostics and succession planning. Our services include business and intangible asset valuation, legal and financial asset assessments, and structured succession planning with tax efficient transmission. By combining technical expertise with strategic insight, we support informed decisions, protect value and ensure smooth asset transfer across generations or business transitions.
heritage.detail: We help clients secure and enhance both professional and personal assets through a service designed to protect value, support strategic decisions and ensure smooth transmission across generations or business transitions. Our approach combines technical expertise, legal insight and financial precision to help individuals, families and organisations manage assets more effectively. Our asset valuation services cover both business and intangible assets, providing reliable assessments that support decisions, transactions, restructuring, reporting and succession planning. We offer heritage diagnostics, including legal and financial asset assessments to identify risks, clarify ownership and strengthen the security of holdings. We also provide succession planning focused on structuring and tax secured transmission, helping clients organise the transfer of wealth or business ownership in an efficient, compliant manner aligned with their objectives. By reducing uncertainty and improving continuity, we help preserve value and protect family or corporate interests.
deliverables: Asset valuation: business and intangible asset valuation.
Heritage diagnostics: legal and financial asset assessments.
Succession planning: structuring and tax secured transmission.

faqs.q: What are two major methods of asset valuation?
faqs.a: Two major methods are the cost method and the market value method. The cost method values an asset based on its original purchase or replacement cost. The market value method estimates what the asset would sell for in the open market. These methods are widely used for business planning, financial reporting, succession planning and investment decisions.

Heritage assets are items of historical, cultural, artistic, scientific or environmental importance. They are often held for public benefit and preserved for future generations rather than mainly for commercial use. They can be difficult to value because of their uniqueness, but still require proper recognition, control and disclosure in financial reporting where applicable.

Business succession planning prepares a company for leadership or ownership transfer when an owner retires, becomes unavailable or exits. It helps maintain stability, protect value and avoid disruption. Good succession planning supports continuity, tax efficiency and long term growth by ensuring the right people and structures are in place.

heritage.keywords: asset valuation methods, heritage assets, succession planning, business transmission

humanCapital.title: Human Capital and Governance Hub
humanCapital.short: We help organisations professionalise teams and governing bodies through tailored training and capacity building. Our services include finance for managers without a finance background, technical coaching for finance teams, and governance training for directors on key regulatory requirements. By strengthening financial understanding, practical skills and board oversight, we support better decisions, improved compliance and stronger institutional performance.
humanCapital.detail: We help organisations professionalise teams and governing bodies through practical training and capacity building designed to improve performance, compliance and leadership. As regulatory expectations rise and financial oversight matters more than ever, strong internal capability is essential for long term success. Our manager training equips those without a finance background with the fundamentals, enabling them to read financial information, understand budgets, interpret key reports and make better operational decisions. We also provide technical coaching for finance teams, strengthening core processes, improving reporting quality and building confidence in day to day financial management, whether the need is budgeting, accounting, internal controls or reporting discipline. For boards and senior leadership, our governance training for directors focuses on regulatory requirements, oversight responsibilities and sound decision making, particularly valuable for institutions seeking stronger governance, clearer accountability and better alignment with legal and compliance obligations. Our approach is practical and targeted, designed to deliver lasting value across teams, management and governing bodies.
deliverables: Manager training: finance for managers without a finance background.
Skills development: technical coaching for finance teams.
Governance training: directors trained on regulatory requirements.

faqs.q: What manager training supports employee growth?
faqs.a: Useful manager training includes leadership development, performance management, communication skills, financial awareness and team coaching. The best programmes help managers improve decision making, support employee development and drive productivity. Good manager training is practical, relevant to your sector and focused on real workplace results rather than theory.

faqs.q: What training is best for managers?
faqs.a: The best training depends on the role, but leadership, communication, delegation, conflict resolution and financial management are among the most valuable. Managers also benefit from strategic thinking, people management and compliance training. Effective management training improves confidence, accountability and team performance.

Governance training is structured learning that helps directors, board members and senior leaders understand their responsibilities, regulatory duties and oversight roles. It covers accountability, compliance, risk management, ethics and internal controls, strengthening board performance, decision making and organisational leadership.

humanCapital.keywords: manager training, governance training, finance for managers, skills development, corporate governance Cameroon

challenges: Regulatory compliance: support across COBAC and related prudential requirements so institutions stay aligned with supervisory expectations.
Risk management: risk mapping, stress testing, liquidity management and operational risk prevention to strengthen resilience.

Portfolio reporting: statutory audits (CAC) and accounting systems diagnostics for reliable, OHADA compliant statements.
Operations: budgeting and monitoring dashboards, variance analysis and accounting engineering for cost control and filings.
Investor relations and risk: risk mapping and financial markets expertise to strengthen governance and stakeholder trust.
assetManagement.frameworks: Our work is aligned with COSUMAF instructions, CAC requirements and OHADA standards.

managementCompanies.title: Management Companies
managementCompanies.description: Under COSUMAF, management companies (sociétés de gestion) are distinct from asset managers: they oversee collective investment vehicles such as mutual funds (FCPs) and open ended investment companies (SICAVs), which are common across the region. We support management companies with COSUMAF compliance audits, internal control systems and independent valuations, alongside statutory audits (CAC) and accounting systems diagnostics for OHADA compliant reporting. Our Performance Hub provides budgeting, dashboards and variance analysis to support fund oversight, transparency and investor confidence.
challenges: COSUMAF compliance: compliance audits, internal controls and independent valuations for collective investment vehicles.
Fund oversight: reliable reporting for FCPs and SICAVs through statutory audits (CAC) and accounting diagnostics.
Transparency: budgeting and variance analysis that support clear, OHADA compliant investor communication.
Governance and risk: internal control reviews and risk mapping to strengthen oversight of collective vehicles.
managementCompanies.frameworks: Our work is aligned with COSUMAF instructions, CAC requirements and OHADA standards.

faq.q: What is the difference between an asset manager and a management company?
faq.a: Asset managers handle the direct management of individual or institutional portfolios, while management companies (sociétés de gestion) oversee collective investment vehicles such as mutual funds (FCPs) and open ended investment companies (SICAVs). Both operate under COSUMAF, and AGILE supports each with compliance audits, internal controls, independent valuations and OHADA compliant reporting.

faqs.a: A statutory audit (CAC) is an annual legal audit required for certain entities, including banks, insurers, microfinance institutions and listed companies. It verifies the reliability of financial information and compliance with applicable laws and standards. Across CEMAC and beyond, statutory audits strengthen transparency, accountability and stakeholder confidence.

Accounting systems diagnostics is a review of an organisation's financial organisation, audit trail and the reliability of its financial statements. It helps identify weaknesses in accounting processes, internal controls and reporting structures. It is essential for improving accuracy, strengthening governance and supporting better decisions.

Contractual audits are independent reviews for specific transactions or engagements, such as acquisition due diligence, project audits and limited reviews. They help organisations assess risk, confirm data reliability and make informed commercial decisions, particularly valuable during investments, partnerships and major projects.

faqs.q: What is SYSCOHADA audit and certification?
faqs.a: SYSCOHADA audit and certification is a specialised service for agro industrial complexes operating under the OHADA framework. It ensures compliance with harmonised accounting standards and supports accurate reporting, helping agro industrial businesses strengthen performance, secure assets and improve credibility with investors, lenders and regulators.

faqs.q: What does collateral security mean in agricultural financing?
faqs.a: Collateral security refers to the legal protection given to lenders through pledged assets in agricultural financing. It helps secure loans and reduce credit risk. Our expertise in securities law supports reliable collateral arrangements that protect both lenders and borrowers while improving access to finance.

faqs.q: What is legal structuring in agro industry?
faqs.a: Legal structuring in agro industry involves drafting value chain contracts and public and private partnership agreements that support commercial relationships and protect business interests. It ensures arrangements are clear, enforceable and aligned with the OHADA framework, improving stability, compliance and long term value creation.

faqs.q: What is an ESG compliance audit?
faqs.a: An ESG compliance audit reviews how environmental, social and governance risks are identified, managed and reported. It helps organisations improve sustainability reporting, strengthen accountability and meet stakeholder expectations. In agro industry and other sectors it supports responsible growth and long term resilience.

COBAC compliance services support banks and microfinance institutions in meeting banking regulatory requirements across CEMAC. These include risk mapping, stress testing, liquidity management and operational risk prevention, helping institutions strengthen prudential control, reduce exposure and improve financial stability.

faqs.q: What are CIMA actuarial and compliance services?
faqs.a: CIMA actuarial and compliance services support insurers with technical provisions review, solvency analysis and actuarial pricing. They help insurers meet regulatory expectations, manage risk and maintain financial soundness, essential for compliance, accurate reporting and long term stability.

Succession planning is the process of structuring and securing the transfer of business or personal assets over time. It includes asset valuation, heritage diagnostics and tax secured transmission, helping protect wealth, reduce conflict and ensure continuity across generations or ownership changes.
